LESSONS CAPTURED BATCH 12:
  ⚖️ Pre-flight router-signature verification is now mandatory. .whatsnext claimed Item 2 would work
  via "existing quotationUpdate" — but the router only accepted top-level fields. Caught this BEFORE
  the BUILD BATCH PROPOSAL was implemented, escalated to user via AskUserQuestion with 3 paths.
  Add to the 6-point pre-flight: "Read the input schema for any router procedure named in .whatsnext."

  ⚖️ The branch-creation line item in the BUILD BATCH PROPOSAL — added as a Batch 11 lesson —
  worked perfectly. Both branches were created with visible TaskUpdate transitions before any
  file write. Rule 23 squash-merge convention is restored as the default flow.

  🟢 Replace-children-in-transaction pattern: for nested draft entities gated to a single status
  with full FK cascades, prefer deleteMany(parents) → cascade-drops-children → recreate from input
  over surgical diff. Avoids per-row create/update/delete plan complexity. Acceptable for ≤100
  child rows. Implementation in apps/web/src/server/trpc/routers/crm.ts quotationUpdate full-payload branch.

  🟢 Inline-base64 signature storage in existing customerSignatureUrl/technicianSignatureUrl
  String columns is acceptable for signature-tier artifacts (≤200KB blobs). Avoids both a schema
  migration and a MinIO upload pipeline. Reconsider only if avg blob >50KB or row count >100K.

  🔴 GOTCHA — `eslint-disable-next-line @next/next/no-img-element` errors when the next eslint
  plugin is not loaded in the project's eslint config. The disable comment itself becomes the error.
  Drop the disable comment when the rule isn't actually configured. Caught and fixed inline in Item 1.

  🔴 GOTCHA — Test-mock convention consistency matters. crm.test.ts mixes `async (args) => value`
  and `(args) => Promise.resolve(value)` for mockImplementation. The async-without-await form trips
  @typescript-eslint/require-await. Grep the test file's existing convention before adding new mocks.
  Caught and fixed inline in Item 2.

LESSONS CAPTURED BATCH 10:
  ⚖️ Opus-direct executor pattern proven 8× consecutive (Batch 5 ×3, 6 ×2, 7 ×2, 8 ×2,
  9 ×2, 10 ×2). Combined per-session safe ceiling holds at ~85-95K for two-item T2/T3
  batches. Pattern is the default for Phase 8 work; only T3+ multi-module rewrites
  should consider Sonnet dispatch or batch splitting.

  🟢 NEW pattern — auto-derived computed cells in Client Component forms keep state
  simple. Quotation Builder's per-line, per-column marked-up price matrix is read-only
  preview computed at render via the same helper that runs at submit time. The user
  only edits baseCost + qty + column %. Submit payload is computed in one pass over
  the current state using the helper. Server stores whatever the client sent. No
  state explosion. Pattern applies to any client form where a derived field can be
  computed deterministically from inputs.

  🟢 NEW pattern — manual migration authoring when DB is offline. `prisma migrate diff`
  needs a reachable shadow DB. When that's unavailable, hand-write the migration SQL
  file using the existing init migration as a template — TEXT/TIMESTAMP(3), DEFAULT
  CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, table_field_idx index naming, ON DELETE CASCADE on cascade
  relationships, ON DELETE RESTRICT on user FK. Prisma migrate dev on next run will
  recognize the migration is already applied (or apply it if not). This unblocks
  schema-touching batches without requiring the user to bring up Docker first.

  🟢 NEW pattern — strict-boolean-expressions fix idiom. For `string | null` fallback
  chains in Next 15 with strict-boolean-expressions ESLint rule: NEVER use truthy
  shortcut `x || y`. Always explicit `x !== null && x.length > 0 ? x : y`. Same for
  `string | undefined`. The linter does not interpret the empty-string falsy rule
  for nullable strings. Caught 7 lint errors on first run of quotation pages; fix
  is mechanical but must be applied at every customer-name/displayName/optional-text
  rendering site.

  ⚖️ Pre-flight schema grep BEFORE the BUILD BATCH PROPOSAL output (the NEW protocol
  from Batch 9) worked again. ContactLog absence was surfaced at proposal time, so
  the migration scope was already factored into the user's confirm decision. Saves
  a confused mid-batch "why isn't this working" cycle. Lesson is now load-bearing.

LESSONS CAPTURED BATCH 9:
  ⚖️ Opus-direct executor pattern proven 7× consecutive (Batch 5 ×3, 6 ×2, 7 ×2, 8 ×2,
  9 ×2). Combined per-session safe ceiling holds at ~65-100K. Pattern is the default
  for Phase 8 T1-T2 work.

  🟢 NEW pattern — pure-helper extraction for client-side forms: extract validation
  + math to a pure TS module (apps/web/src/lib/pos-cart.ts) and unit-test it directly
  in node-env vitest. The React Client Component becomes a thin wrapper around the
  helpers — typecheck + lint verify correctness without needing jsdom. Pattern applies
  to ANY Client Component with non-trivial validation (cart, quotation builder, multi-
  step form). The cart math suite (22 tests) caught zero bugs but locks the contract
  so future refactors of cart-client.tsx don't drift from the server-side rules.

  🟢 NEW pattern — schema-driven scope adjustment at PROPOSAL time. .whatsnext
  recommended ContactLog + Quotation. Pre-flight grep on schema.prisma revealed
  ContactLog model does not exist (would need migration) while Quotation has 6
  models already in place. Proposed swap at the BUILD BATCH PROPOSAL output, user
  confirmed, batch proceeded with richer scope coverage. Lesson: pre-flight grep on
  the schema BEFORE the proposal is non-optional — it can collapse OR expand scope
  significantly and the user should see the corrected scope before committing.

  🟢 Decimal → number serialization needed at the Server → Client Component boundary.
  Prisma returns Decimal; Client Components receive props via JSON serialization which
  doesn't preserve Decimal. Convert in the Server Component before passing.

  🟢 Atomic multi-table writes with caller-supplied index references work cleanly
  inside a $transaction: build a parallel array of created IDs during transaction
  execution (markupColumnIds[]), then resolve the index → ID lookup when creating
  the child rows. Cleaner than client-supplied IDs that would have to be validated
  against the just-created records.

  ⚖️ Pre-flight schema read (lines 486-600 of schema.prisma) BEFORE writing the
  quotation router prevented all field-name drift. First typecheck attempt was clean.
  Lesson holds across the batch: schema-driven code starts with reading the schema.

LESSONS CAPTURED BATCH 8:
  ⚖️ Opus-direct executor pattern proven 6× consecutive now (Batch 5 ×3, Batch 6 ×2,
  Batch 7 ×2, Batch 8 ×2). Pattern is the default for Phase 8 T1-T2 work. Combined
  per-session safe ceiling holds at ~85-100K — Batch 8 was smaller than that ceiling
  by design because of pre-flight scope reduction.

  🔴 NEW gotcha — diagnostic discipline: `tsc <specific-file>` BYPASSES tsconfig.json
  and uses TypeScript defaults. This produces MISLEADING moduleResolution errors on
  workspace imports (the apps/worker pre-flight in this batch initially diagnosed
  "moduleResolution = bundler needed" when the real bug was a test fixture missing
  4 required type fields). ALWAYS use `pnpm typecheck` for triage. NEVER pass file
  paths directly to tsc when investigating tsconfig-related issues.

  🟢 Transitive peer deps don't symlink in pnpm. @tanstack/react-query was resolved
  by pnpm as a transitive peer of @trpc/react-query (visible in pnpm-lock.yaml) but
  NOT symlinked into apps/web/node_modules. node could not require() it, TypeScript
  could not resolve imports from it. Direct deps must be in package.json even when
  a peer-dep range covers them. Verify with `node -e "require.resolve('pkg')"` from
  the consuming app dir BEFORE writing imports.

  🟢 tRPC v11 createClient returns a callable Proxy (typeof === 'function'), not a
  plain object. Test assertions on the client surface must use 'function' not 'object'.

  🟢 Provider tests in vitest node environment (globals:false): can't render React.
  Smoke tests on module exports + client-side createClient surface are sufficient.
  Actual hook behavior is tested implicitly by every future Client Component that
  uses the Provider — no need for jsdom switch.

  ⚖️ Pre-flight saved real time. Discovered scope-shrinking facts BEFORE committing
  to estimate: @trpc/* packages already installed, only @tanstack missing as direct
  dep, worker error was test data not config. Lesson: package.json + node_modules
  + actual error reproduction (NOT diagnostic shortcuts) should always run before
  the Phase 8 scope estimate is finalized.

LESSONS CAPTURED BATCH 7:
  ⚖️ Opus-direct executor pattern proven 5× consecutive now (Batch 5 ×3, Batch 6 ×2, Batch 7 ×2).
  Two T2 items (~25K + ~45K) merged cleanly in a single continuous session with
  ZERO thrash, ZERO retry, ZERO Sonnet dispatch. Pattern is now load-bearing default
  for Phase 8 T2 work. Current win streak suggests safe upper bound of ~85-100K
  combined per session.

  🔴 Pre-flight code-pattern check is non-optional. Discovered NO tRPC React client
  exists in codebase before writing any cart UI. Saved an entire half-batch worth
  of effort that would have produced infrastructure-coupled code with nowhere to
  land. NEW PROTOCOL: when an item involves "interactive UI" or "client component
  talking to mutations", grep for `useMutation\|useQuery\|createTRPCReact` BEFORE
  scoping. If absent, the item is actually two items (infra batch + consumer batch).

  🟡 Test mock leak across describe blocks. New describe blocks added to a file
  whose existing convention puts `beforeEach(vi.clearAllMocks)` per-describe (not
  top-level) WILL leak mock.calls across tests. Symptom: `mock.calls[0][0]` returns
  the first call from a PRIOR test in the file, not the first call in the current
  test. Fix: copy the per-describe beforeEach pattern when extending such files.
  Better: use `toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.objectContaining(...))` instead of
  `mock.calls[0][0]` indexing — survives mock-leak issues AND TS strict-mode.

  🟢 mockImplementation(async (fn) => fn(mockDb)) is a stronger transaction-test
  pattern than mockResolvedValue because it actually invokes the inner callback
  body — proving fundTransaction.create + fundSource.update were both called inside
  the transaction, not just that $transaction was called. Worth the per-file
  eslint-disable expansion (no-explicit-any + require-await + no-unsafe-return/call).

  🟢 Schema verified `refund` and `adjustment` are valid FundTransaction.type values
  per existing enum comment in schema.prisma — no new migration needed for either
  Phase 2b mutation. Pattern: when a router needs new types, check the existing
  type enum comment in the schema BEFORE proposing migrations.

  by Opus in a single session, no thrash, no retry. Validates the rule from Item 3
  lessons. Apply same rule to Items 2 + 3 — if scope >4 files, skip Sonnet dispatch
  ceremony entirely.

  🔴 Untracked draft routers from prior sessions accumulate drift faster than active
  work — the May 11 Support router had 4 distinct schema-drift bugs (tenantId filters,
  fake @prisma/client enums, missing relation, fake User.name field) that all surfaced
  only at typecheck. NEW PROTOCOL: when continuing in-flight work from a prior session,
  run `pnpm typecheck` BEFORE writing tests or UI on top of the draft — treat untracked
  router files as Sonnet-quality output requiring Opus verification.

  🔴 `User.name` recurrence — Batch 4+5 has had this drift 3 times now. Locking the
  canonical User select shape: `{ id: true, firstName: true, lastName: true, displayName: true }`
  plus UI helper `userDisplayName(u) = u.displayName ?? "${u.firstName} ${u.lastName}".trim()`.
  Pre-flight checklist for Items 2 + 3 must include this shape.

CARRIED-FORWARD LESSON FROM BATCH 4 ITEM 3 (still valid):
  Sonnet thrash is NOT bounded by verification step alone. Empirical thresholds:
  Item 1 = 44 tools (combined task), Item 2 = 11 tools both passes (verification),
  Item 3 = 24 tools (writes-only, larger prompt, 6 files). Rule stands: dispatch
  ≤4 files per Sonnet call. 5+ files → Opus executor up front per §1 Step 2.5b.

Schema-vs-spec drift remained the BIGGEST source of post-write fixes across all 3 Items
of Batch 4 (Item 1: User.name×5 / Item 2: ProjectExpense schema / Item 3: Vendor.companyName +
PO.taxAmount + User.name + GoodsReceiptItem.no-allocationId). Even with explicit pre-flight
grep + schema fields pre-inlined in dispatch, Sonnet hallucinated field names. NEW RULE:
pre-inline ALL schema fields in test FIXTURE FORMAT (so Sonnet copies-not-derives), not
just narrative description in the prompt body.
